items.src: Al-Bukhari 5/172

chapters.title: Supplication of one who fears the oppression of a ruler

items.ar: اللهم رب السموات السبع ،ورب العرش العظيم ،كن لي جاراً من فلان بن فلان ، وأحزابه من خلائقك ؛ أن يفرط على أحد منهم أو يطغى ، عز جارك ،وجل ثناؤك ،ولا إله إلا أنت
items.text: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, be my protector against so-and-so son of so-and-so and his allies among Your creatures, lest any of them act hastily against me or transgress. Mighty is the one under Your protection, majestic is Your praise, and there is no god but You.
items.src: Al-Bukhari in «al-Adab al-Mufrad», no. 707; graded authentic by al-Albani in «Sahih al-Adab al-Mufrad», no. 545

items.ar: الله أكبر، الله أعز من خلقه جميعاً ، الله أعز مما أخاف وأحذر ،أعوذ بالله الذي لا إله إلا هو ، الممسك السموات السبع أن يقعن على الأرض إلا بإذنه ،من شر عبدك فلان ،وجنوده وأتباعه وأشياعه ، من الجن والأنس ، اللهم كن لي جاراً من شرهم ، جل ثناؤك وعز جارك ، وتبارك اسمك ، ولا إله غيرك  ( ثلاث مرات )
items.text: Allah is the Greatest. Allah is mightier than all His creation. Allah is mightier than what I fear and dread. I seek refuge in Allah, besides whom there is no god, who holds back the seven heavens from falling upon the earth except by His permission, from the evil of Your servant so-and-so, and his soldiers, followers and partisans among the jinn and mankind. O Allah, be my protector against their evil. Majestic is Your praise, mighty is the one under Your protection, blessed is Your name, and there is no god other than You. (Three times)
items.src: Al-Bukhari in «al-Adab al-Mufrad», no. 708; graded authentic by al-Albani in «Sahih al-Adab al-Mufrad», no.

chapters.title: Supplication against the enemy

items.ar: اللهم منزل الكتاب ، سريع الحساب ،اهزم الأحزاب ،اللهم اهزمهم وزلزلهم
items.text: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Swift in reckoning, defeat the confederates. O Allah, defeat them and shake them.
items.src: Muslim 3/1362

chapters.title: What to say when one fears a people

items.ar: اللهم اكفنيهم بما شئت
items.text: O Allah, suffice me against them with whatever You will.
items.src: Muslim 4/2300

chapters.title: Supplication of one afflicted with doubt in faith
chapters.titleAr: دعاء من أصابه شك في الإيمان

items.ar: يستعيذ بالله
items.text: He seeks refuge in Allah.
items.src: Al-Bukhari (with al-Fath) 6/336 and Muslim 1/120

items.ar: ينتهي عما شك فيه
items.text: He stops dwelling on what he has doubts about.
items.src: Al-Bukhari (with al-Fath) 6/336 and Muslim 1/120

items.ar: يقول آمنت بالله ورسله
items.text: He says: «I believe in Allah and His messengers.»
items.src: Muslim 1/120

items.ar: يقرأ قوله تعالى { هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ }
items.text: He recites the saying of the Exalted: «He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has full knowledge of all things.»
items.src: Surat al-Hadid, verse 3. Abu Dawud 4/329; graded hasan by al-Albani in «Sahih Abi Dawud» 3/962

chapters.title: Supplication for settling a debt

items.ar: اللهم اكفني بحلالك عن حرامك ، وأغنني بفضلك عمن سواك
items.text: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have made unlawful, and by Your bounty make me independent of all besides You.
items.src: At-Tirmidhi 5/560; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/180

items.ar: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الهم والحزن ، والعجز والكسل ،والبخل والجبن وضلع الدين وغلبة الرجال
items.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men.
items.src: Al-Bukhari 7/158

chapters.title: Supplication against whisperings in prayer and recitation

items.ar: أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم واتفل على يسارك ( ثلاثاً )
items.text: «I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed» — and spit lightly to your left (three times).
items.src: Muslim 4/1729, from the hadith of 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, in which he said: «I did that, and Allah removed it from me»

chapters.title: Supplication of one who finds a matter difficult

items.ar: اللهم لا سهل إلا ما جعلته سهلاً وأنت تجعل الحزن إذا شئت سهلاً
items.text: O Allah, nothing is easy except what You make easy, and You make the difficult easy if You will.
items.src: Reported by Ibn Hibban in his «Sahih», no. 2427 (Mawarid), and Ibn as-Sunni, no. 351. Al-Hafiz said: «This is an authentic hadith.» 'Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut graded it authentic in his takhrij of an-Nawawi's «al-Adhkar», p. 106

chapters.title: What one says and does after committing a sin
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول ويفعل من أذنب ذنباً

items.ar: ما من عبدٍ يذنب ذنباً فيحسن الطهور ، ثم يقوم فيصلي ركعتين ، ثم يستغفر الله إلا غفر الله لهُ
items.text: There is no servant who commits a sin, then purifies himself well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs, then asks Allah for forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him.
items.src: Abu Dawud 2/86 and at-Tirmidhi 2/257; graded authentic by al-Albani in «Sahih Abi Dawud» 1/283

chapters.title: Supplication for repelling Satan and his whisperings

items.ar: الاستعاذة بالله منه
items.text: Seeking refuge in Allah from him.
items.src: Abu Dawud 1/206 and at-Tirmidhi; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 1/77, and see Surat al-Mu'minun, verses 98–99

items.ar: الأذان
items.text: The adhan (call to prayer).
items.src: Muslim 1/291 and al-Bukhari 1/151

items.ar: الأذكار وقراءة القرآن
items.text: Words of remembrance and recitation of the Qur'an.
items.src: «Do not make your houses graves. Indeed, Satan flees from the house in which Surat al-Baqarah is recited.» Reported by Muslim 1/539. Among the things that repel Satan are the morning and evening adhkar, the adhkar of sleeping and waking, the adhkar of entering and leaving the home, the adhkar of entering and leaving the mosque, and other legislated adhkar, such as reciting Ayat al-Kursi at bedtime and the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah. Whoever says one hundred times: «There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent», it will be a protection for him from Satan for that whole day. Likewise the adhan repels Satan

chapters.title: Supplication when something displeasing happens or one is overwhelmed by a matter
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء حينما يقع مالا يرضاه أو غلب على أمره

items.ar: قدر الله وما شاء فعل
items.text: Allah has decreed, and what He willed He did.
items.src: «The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and in each there is good. Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say: “If only I had done such-and-such”; rather say: “Allah has decreed, and what He willed He did”, for “if only” opens the door to the work of Satan.» Muslim 4/2052

items.ar: إذا غلبك أمر فقل :  حسبي الله ونعم الوكيل
items.text: If a matter overwhelms you, say: «Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.»
items.src: See al-Arna'ut's takhrij of «al-Adhkar», p. 106

chapters.title: Congratulating on the birth of a child, and the reply

items.ar: بارك الله لك في الموهوب لك ،وشكرت الواهب، وبلغ أشدهُ، ورزقت برهُ  .ويردُ عليه المهنأ فيقول :  بارك الله لك وبارك عليك ، وجزاك الله خيراً ، ورزقك الله مثله، وأجزل ثوابك
items.text: «May Allah bless for you what has been granted to you; may you be grateful to the Giver; may he reach maturity; and may you be granted his dutifulness.» And the one who is congratulated replies, saying: «May Allah bless you and bestow blessings upon you, may Allah reward you with good, may Allah grant you the like of it, and may He make your reward abundant.»
items.src: See an-Nawawi, «al-Adhkar», p. 349, and Salim al-Hilali, «Sahih al-Adhkar li-n-Nawawi» 2/713

chapters.title: Seeking protection for children

items.ar: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعوذ الحسن والحسين أعيذكما بكلمات الله التامة ، من كل شيطان وهامة ، ومن كل عينِ لامة
items.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek protection for al-Hasan and al-Husayn (saying): «I seek protection for you both in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every poisonous creature, and from every evil eye.»
items.src: Al-Bukhari 4/119, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both

chapters.title: Supplication for the sick when visiting them

items.ar: لا بأس طهور إن شاء الله
items.text: No harm; it is a purification, if Allah wills.
items.src: Al-Bukhari (with al-Fath) 10/118

items.ar: أسأل الله العظيم رب العرش العظيم أن يشفيك ( سبع مرات )
items.text: I ask Allah the Mighty, Lord of the Mighty Throne, to cure you. (Seven times)
items.src: There is no Muslim servant who visits a sick person whose appointed time has not yet come and says seven times: ... (the hadith), except that he will be cured. Reported by at-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud. See Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2/210 and «Sahih al-Jami'» 5/180

chapters.title: The virtue of visiting the sick

items.ar: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : إذا عاد الرجل أخاه المسلم مشى في خرافة الجنة حتى يجلس فإذا جلس غمرته الرحمة ، فإن كان غدوة صلى عليه سبعون ألف ملك حتى يمسي ، وإن كان مساء صلى عليه سبعون ألف ملك حتى يصبح
items.text: He ﷺ said: «When a man visits his sick Muslim brother, he walks among the harvest of Paradise until he sits. When he sits, mercy envelops him. If it is in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until evening, and if it is in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until morning.»
items.src: Reported by at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ahmad. See Sahih Ibn Majah 1/244 and Sahih at-Tirmidhi 1/286; Ahmad Shakir also graded it authentic

chapters.title: Supplication of the sick person who has despaired of life
chapters.titleAr: دعاء المريض الذي يئس من حياته

items.ar: اللهم اغفر لي وارحمني والحقني بالرفيق الأعلى
items.text: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the Highest Companion.
items.src: Al-Bukhari 7/10 and Muslim 4/1893

items.ar: جعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يدخل يديه في الماء فيمسح بهما وجههُ ويقول : لا إله إلا الله إن للموت لسكرات
items.text: The Prophet ﷺ began putting his hands into water and wiping his face with them, saying: «There is no god but Allah; indeed death has its agonies.»
items.src: Al-Bukhari (with al-Fath) 8/144; the hadith also mentions the siwak

items.ar: لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ، لا إله إلا الله وحده ، لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك لهُ ، لا إله إلا الله لهُ الملك ولهُ الحمد ، لا إله إلا الله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
items.text: There is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah alone. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. There is no god but Allah; His is the dominion and His is the praise. There is no god but Allah, and there is no might nor power except by Allah.
items.src: Reported by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, and graded authentic by al-Albani. See Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/152 and Sahih Ibn Majah 2/317

chapters.title: Prompting the dying person (talqin)

items.ar: من كان آخر كلامه لا إله إلا الله دخل الجنة
items.text: Whoever's last words are «There is no god but Allah» will enter Paradise.
items.src: Abu Dawud 3/190; see «Sahih al-Jami'» 5/432

chapters.title: Supplication of one struck by a calamity

items.ar: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون اللهم أجرني في مصيبتي وأخلف لي خيراً منها
items.text: Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we shall return. O Allah, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better.
items.src: Muslim 2/632

chapters.title: Supplication when closing the eyes of the deceased

items.ar: اللهم اغفر  لفلان ( باسمه ) ورفع درجته في المهديين، واخلفه في عقبه في الغابرين، واغفر لنا وله يا رب العالمين ،وافسح له في قبره ونور له فيه
items.text: O Allah, forgive so-and-so (mentioning his name), raise his rank among the rightly guided, be a successor to him among those he leaves behind, forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds, make his grave spacious for him and give him light in it.
items.src: Muslim 2/634

chapters.title: Supplication for the deceased in the funeral prayer

items.ar: اللهم اغفر له وارحمه، وعافه ،واعف عنه ،وأكرم نُزُله ، ووسع مُدخلهُ ، واغسله بالماء والثلج والبرد ، ونقه من الخطايا كما ينقى الثوب الأبيض من الدنس ، وأبدله داراً خيراً من داره ، وأهلاً خيراً من أهله وزوجاً خيراً من زوجه، وأدخله الجنة ،وأعذه من عذاب القبر ( ومن عذاب النار )
items.text: O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him, keep him safe and pardon him; honour his reception and make his entrance wide; wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. Give him a home better than his home, a family better than his family and a spouse better than his spouse. Admit him into Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave (and from the punishment of the Fire).
items.src: Muslim 2/663

items.ar: اللهم اغفر لحينا وميتنا ، وشاهدنا وغائبنا ، وصغيرنا وكبيرنا ، وذكرنا وأُنثانا ، اللهم من أحييته منا فأحيه على الإسلام ، ومن توفيته منا فتوفه على الإيمان ، اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تضلنا بعده
items.text: O Allah, forgive our living and our dead, those present and those absent, our young and our old, our males and our females. O Allah, whomever of us You keep alive, keep him alive upon Islam, and whomever of us You take, take him upon faith. O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not lead us astray after him.
items.src: Ibn Majah 1/480 and Ahmad 2/368; see Sahih Ibn Majah 1/251

items.ar: اللهم إن فلان بن فلان في ذمتك،وحبل جوارك،فقه من فتنة القبر وعذاب النار،وأنت أهل الوفاء والحق .فاغفر له وارحمهُ إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم
items.text: O Allah, so-and-so son of so-and-so is in Your care and under the rope of Your protection, so protect him from the trial of the grave and the punishment of the Fire. You are the One worthy of faithfulness and truth. So forgive him and have mercy on him; indeed You are the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
items.src: Reported by Ibn Majah; see Sahih Ibn Majah 1/251; also narrated by Abu Dawud 3/211

items.ar: اللهم عبدك وابن عبدك وابن أمتك احتاج إلى رحمتك ،وأنت غني عن عذابه،إن كان مُحسناً فزده في حسناته، وإن كان مُسيئاً فتجاوز عنه
items.text: O Allah, (this is) Your servant, the son of Your servant and the son of Your maidservant. He is in need of Your mercy, and You have no need to punish him. If he was a doer of good, increase his good deeds, and if he was a wrongdoer, overlook his misdeeds.
items.src: Reported by al-Hakim, who graded it authentic, and adh-Dhahabi agreed with him 1/359. See al-Albani, «Ahkam al-Jana'iz», p. 125

chapters.title: Supplication for a deceased child in the funeral prayer

items.ar: اللهم أعذه من عذاب القبر
items.text: O Allah, protect him from the punishment of the grave.
items.src: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: «I prayed behind Abu Hurayrah over a child who had never committed a sin, and I heard him say: ...» (the hadith). Reported by Malik in «al-Muwatta'» 1/288, Ibn Abi Shaybah in «al-Musannaf» 3/217 and al-Bayhaqi 4/9; Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut graded its chain authentic in his edition of al-Baghawi's «Sharh as-Sunnah» 5/357

items.ar: أن قال : اللهم اجعله فرطاً وذخراً لوالديه ،وشفيعاً مجاباً .اللهم ثقل به موازينها وأعظم به أجورهما ، وألحقهُ بصالح المؤمنين ، واجعلهُ في كفالة إبراهيم ، وقه برحمتك عذاب الجحيم ، وأبدله داراً خيراً من داره ، وأهلاً خيراً من أهله ، اللهم اغفر لاسلافنا ، وأفراطنا ، ومن سبقنا بالإيمان  فحسن
items.text: If he says: «O Allah, make him a forerunner and a stored treasure for his parents, and an intercessor whose intercession is accepted. O Allah, through him make their scales heavy and their rewards great; join him with the righteous believers, place him in the care of Ibrahim, protect him by Your mercy from the punishment of Hellfire, and give him a home better than his home and a family better than his family. O Allah, forgive our predecessors, our children who went before us, and those who preceded us in faith» — that is good.
items.src: See Ibn Qudamah, «al-Mughni» 3/416, and Shaykh 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Baz (may Allah preserve him), «ad-Durus al-Muhimmah li-'Ammat al-Ummah», p. 15

items.ar: اللهم اجعله لنا فرطاً ،وسلفاً وأجراً
items.text: O Allah, make him for us a forerunner, a predecessor and a reward.
items.src: Al-Hasan used to recite the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah) over a child and say: ... (the hadith). Reported by al-Baghawi in «Sharh as-Sunnah» 5/357 and 'Abd ar-Razzaq, no. 6588; al-Bukhari mentioned it without a chain (mu'allaq) in the Book of Funerals, chapter 65, «Reciting the Opening of the Book over the deceased» 2/113

chapters.title: Supplication of condolence

items.ar: إن لله ما أخذ وله ما أعطى . وكل شيء عنده بأجل مُسمى ...فلتصبر ولتحتسب
items.text: Indeed, to Allah belongs what He took, and to Him belongs what He gave, and everything with Him has an appointed term... so let her be patient and seek the reward from Allah.
items.src: al-Bukhari 2/80, Muslim 2/636

items.ar: وإن قال :  أعظم الله أجرك ،وأحسن عزاءك وغفر لميتك  فحسن
items.text: And if he says: «May Allah make your reward great, make your consolation good, and forgive your deceased», that is good.
items.src: al-Adhkar by an-Nawawi, p. 126

chapters.title: Supplication when placing the deceased in the grave

items.ar: بسم الله وعلى سُنة رسول الله
items.text: In the name of Allah and according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah.
items.src: Abu Dawud 3/314 with a sahih chain; and Ahmad with the wording: «In the name of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah», and its chain is sahih.

chapters.title: Supplication after burying the deceased

items.ar: اللهم اغفر له اللهم ثبته
items.text: O Allah, forgive him! O Allah, make him firm!
items.src: When the Prophet ﷺ finished burying the deceased, he would stand over him and say: «Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask that he be made firm, for he is now being questioned.» Abu Dawud 3/315; al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, and adh-Dhahabi agreed, 1/370.

chapters.title: Supplication when visiting graves

items.ar: السلام عليكم أهل الديار ، من المؤمنين والمسلمين، وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون [ ويرحم الله المُستقدمين منا والمستأخرين ] أسأل الله لنا ولكم العافية
items.text: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the dwellings, from among the believers and the Muslims. And we, if Allah wills, shall join you. [May Allah have mercy on those of us who have gone ahead and those who come later.] I ask Allah for well-being for us and for you.
items.src: Muslim 2/671, and Ibn Majah (the wording is his) 1/494, from Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him); what is between the square brackets is from the hadith of Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) in Muslim 2/671.

chapters.title: Supplication when the wind blows

items.ar: اللهم إني أسألك خيرها ، وأعوذ بك من شرها
items.text: O Allah, I ask You for its good, and I seek refuge in You from its evil.
items.src: Abu Dawud 4/326 and Ibn Majah 2/1228; see Sahih Ibn Majah 2/305.

items.ar: اللهم إني أسألك خيرها ، وخير ما فيها ، وخير ما أُرسلت به ، وأعوذ بك من شرها وشر ما فيها وشر ما أرسلت به
items.text: O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good of what it contains, and the good of what it has been sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of what it contains, and the evil of what it has been sent with.
items.src: Muslim 2/616, al-Bukhari 4/76

chapters.title: Supplication upon hearing thunder

items.ar: سبحان الذي يُسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته
items.text: Glory be to Him Whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels (too) out of fear of Him.
items.src: When Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both) heard thunder, he would stop speaking and say: .... al-Muwatta 2/992; al-Albani said: its chain is sahih as mawquf (a saying of the Companion).

chapters.title: Some supplications for rain

items.ar: اللهم اسقنا غيثاً مغيثاً مريئاً مَريعاً نافعاً غير ضار ، عاجلاً غير آجل
items.text: O Allah, give us rain: relieving, wholesome, abundant, beneficial and not harmful, swift and not delayed.
items.src: Abu Dawud 1/303; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/216.

items.ar: اللهم أغثنا ، اللهم أغثنا ، اللهم أغثنا
items.text: O Allah, send us rain! O Allah, send us rain! O Allah, send us rain!
items.src: al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 2/613

items.ar: اللهم اسق عبادك وبهائمك ، وانشر رحمتك وأحيي بلدك الميت
items.text: O Allah, give water to Your servants and Your livestock, spread Your mercy, and revive Your dead land.
items.src: Abu Dawud 1/305; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/218.

chapters.title: Supplication when it rains

items.ar: اللهم صيباً نافعاً
items.text: O Allah, (make it) a beneficial rain!
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 2/518

chapters.title: Remembrance after rain

items.ar: مُطرنا بفضل الله ورحمته
items.text: We have been given rain by the bounty of Allah and His mercy.
items.src: al-Bukhari 1/205, Muslim 1/83

chapters.title: Some supplications for the rain to stop

items.ar: اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا ، اللهم على الآكامِ والظرابِ وبُطون الأودية ، ومنابت الشجر
items.text: O Allah, around us and not upon us! O Allah, upon the hillocks, the mounds, the bottoms of the valleys, and the places where trees grow!
items.src: al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 2/614

chapters.title: Supplication upon sighting the new moon

items.ar: الله أكبر ،اللهم أهلِه علينا بالأمن والإيمان ، والسلامة والإسلام ،والتوفيق لما تحب ربنا وترضى ، ربنا وربك الله
items.text: Allah is the Greatest! O Allah, bring it over us with security and faith, with safety and Islam, and with success in what You love and are pleased with, our Lord. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/504, and ad-Darimi with this wording 1/336; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/157.

chapters.title: Supplication of the fasting person when breaking the fast

items.ar: ذَهبَ الظَّمأُ، وابتلَّت العروقُ وثَبَتَ الأجرُ إنْ شاء الله
items.text: The thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.
items.src: Abu Dawud 2/306 and others; see Sahih al-Jami' 4/209.

items.ar: اللهم إني أسألك برحمتك التي وسعت كل شيءٍ أن تغفر لي
items.text: O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy, which encompasses all things, that You forgive me.
items.src: Ibn Majah 1/557, from the supplication of Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both); al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) graded it hasan in Takhrij al-Adhkar; see Sharh al-Adhkar 4/342.

chapters.title: Supplication before eating

items.ar: إذا أكل أحدكم الطعام فليقل: بِسم الله، فإن نسي في أوله فليقل: بِسمِ الله في أوله وآخره
items.text: When one of you eats food, let him say: «In the name of Allah». If he forgets at its beginning, let him say: «In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end».
items.src: Abu Dawud 3/347, at-Tirmidhi 4/288; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2/167.

items.ar: من أطعمه الله الطعام فليقل: اللهم بارك لنا فيه وأطعمنا خيراً منه. ومن سقاه الله لبناً فليقل: اللهم بارك لنا فيه وزدنا منه
items.text: Whomever Allah feeds with food, let him say: «O Allah, bless it for us and feed us with better than it». And whomever Allah gives milk to drink, let him say: «O Allah, bless it for us and give us more of it».
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/506; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/158.

chapters.title: Supplication upon finishing a meal

items.ar: الحمد لله الذي أطعمني هذا ،وزرقنيه ،من غير حول مني ولا قوة
items.text: Praise be to Allah Who fed me this and provided it for me without any might or power on my part.
items.src: Reported by the compilers of the Sunan except an-Nasa'i; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/159.

items.ar: الحمدُ لله حمداً كثيراً طيباً مباركاً فيهِ، غيْرَ [مَكْفيٍّ ولا] مُوَدَّع، ولا مُستَغنَى عَنْهُ ربّنا
items.text: Praise be to Allah, abundant, good and blessed praise, [never sufficient, and] never bidding farewell, and never dispensed with, our Lord.
items.src: al-Bukhari 6/214, and at-Tirmidhi with this wording 5/507

chapters.title: The guest's supplication for the host

items.ar: اللهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَهُم فيما رَزَقتهْمْ، واغْفِر لهم وارحَمْهُم
items.text: O Allah, bless them in what You have provided them, forgive them and have mercy on them.
items.src: Muslim 3/1626

chapters.title: Supplication for one who gives you drink, or when you want that
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء لمن سقاه أو إذا أراد ذلك

items.ar: اللهُمَّ أَطْعِمْ مَنْ أطْعَمَني وأَسْقِ مَنْ سْقَاني
items.text: O Allah, feed whoever fed me and give drink to whoever gave me drink.
items.src: Muslim 3/26

chapters.title: Supplication when breaking the fast with a family
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء إذا أفطر عند أهل بيت

items.ar: أَفطَر عِنْدَكُم الصائِمونَ ، وأكل طعامَكُمُ الأبْرارُ ، وصلت عليكُمُ الملائِكَةُ
items.text: May fasting people break their fast with you, may the righteous eat your food, and may the angels send blessings upon you.
items.src: Sunan Abi Dawud 3/367, Ibn Majah 1/556, and an-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah no. 298, who stated that he ﷺ would say it when he broke his fast with a family; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih Abi Dawud 2/730.

chapters.title: Supplication of the fasting person when food is presented and he does not break his fast
chapters.titleAr: دعاء الصائم إذا حضر الطعام ولم يفطر

items.ar: إذا دُعي أحدكم فليجب ، فإن كان صائماً فليصل وإن كان مفطراً فليطعم  ومعنى فليصل أي فليدع
items.text: When one of you is invited, let him accept. If he is fasting, let him «pray», and if he is not fasting, let him eat. The meaning of «let him pray» is: let him supplicate.
items.src: Muslim 2/1054

chapters.title: What the fasting person says when someone insults him
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول الصائم إذا سابه أحد

items.ar: إني صائم ، إني صائم
items.text: I am fasting, I am fasting.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 4/103, Muslim 2/806

chapters.title: Supplication upon seeing the first fruits

items.ar: اللهم بارك لنا في ثمرنا ، وبارك لنا في مدينتنا وبارك لنا في صاعنا ، وبارك لنا في مدنا
items.text: O Allah, bless us in our fruits, bless us in our city, bless us in our sa', and bless us in our mudd.
items.src: Muslim 2/1000

chapters.title: Supplication when sneezing

items.ar: إذا عطس أحدكم فليقل الحمد لله ،وليقل له أخوهُ أو صاحبهُ : يرحمك الله ،فإذا قال لهُ :يرحمك الله ،فليقل :يهديكم الله ويصلح بالكم
items.text: When one of you sneezes, let him say: «Praise be to Allah», and let his brother or companion say to him: «May Allah have mercy on you». And when he says to him: «May Allah have mercy on you», let him say: «May Allah guide you and set right your affairs».
items.src: al-Bukhari 7/125

chapters.title: What is said to a disbeliever who sneezes and praises Allah
chapters.titleAr: ما يقالُ للكافر إذا عطس فحمد الله

items.ar: يهديكم الله ويصلح بالكم
items.text: May Allah guide you and set right your affairs.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/82, Ahmad 4/400, Abu Dawud 4/308; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2/354.

chapters.title: Supplication for the newly married

items.ar: بارك الله لك ، وبارك عليك ، وجمع بينكما في خير
items.text: May Allah bless you, send blessings upon you, and unite you both in goodness.
items.src: Reported by the compilers of the Sunan except an-Nasa'i; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 1/316.

chapters.title: Supplication of the newly married for himself, and upon buying an animal
chapters.titleAr: دعاء المتزوج لنفسه ودعاء شراء الدابة

items.ar: إذا تزوج أحدكم امرأة ،أو إذا اشترى خادماً فليقل : اللهم إني أسألك خيرها وخير ما جبلتها عليه وأعوذ بك من شرها وشر ما جبلتها عليه ، وإذا اشترى بعيراً فليأخذ بذروة سنامه وليقل مثل ذلك
items.text: When one of you marries a woman or buys a servant, let him say: «O Allah, I ask You for her good and the good of the nature You have created her with, and I seek refuge in You from her evil and the evil of the nature You have created her with». And when he buys a camel, let him take hold of the top of its hump and say the same.
items.src: Abu Dawud 2/248, Ibn Majah 1/617; see Sahih Ibn Majah 1/324.

chapters.title: Supplication before intimacy with one's wife

items.ar: بسم الله ، اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا
items.text: In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep the Shaytan away from us and keep the Shaytan away from what You provide us.
items.src: al-Bukhari 6/141, Muslim 2/1028

chapters.title: Supplication when angry

items.ar: أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم
items.text: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.
items.src: al-Bukhari 6/99, Muslim 4/2015

chapters.title: Supplication upon seeing someone afflicted

items.ar: الحمد لله الذي عافاني مما ابتلاك به ، وفضلني على كثير ممن خلق تفضيلاً
items.text: Praise be to Allah Who has spared me from what He has afflicted you with, and has greatly favoured me over many of those He has created.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/494 and 5/493; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/153.

chapters.title: What is said in a gathering

items.ar: عن ابن عمر قال : كان يعد لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المجلس الواحد مائة مرة من قبل أن يقوم رب اغفر لي وتب علي إنك أنت التواب الغفور
items.text: Ibn Umar said: It used to be counted that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say a hundred times in a single sitting, before he got up: «My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; indeed, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Forgiving».
items.src: at-Tirmidhi and others; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/153 and Sahih Ibn Majah 2/321; the wording is at-Tirmidhi's.

chapters.title: Expiation of a gathering, and what gatherings are concluded with

items.ar: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك ، أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أستغفرك وأتوب إليك
items.text: Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.
items.src: Reported by the compilers of the Sunan; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/153. It is authentically established that Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never sat in a gathering, recited Qur'an or performed a prayer without concluding it with some words...» the hadith. Reported by an-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah no. 308 and Ahmad 6/77; Dr. Faruq Hamadah graded it sahih in his edition of an-Nasa'i's 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah, p. 273.

chapters.title: Supplication for one who says: May Allah forgive you
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء لمن قال غفر الله لك

items.ar: ولك
items.text: And you (too).
items.src: Ahmad 5/28, and an-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah p. 218 no. 421, edited by Dr. Faruq Hamadah.

chapters.title: Supplication for one who does you a favour

items.ar: جَزَاكَ الله خيراً
items.text: May Allah reward you with good.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi no. 2035; see Sahih al-Jami' 6244 and Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2/200.

chapters.title: What protects from the Dajjal

items.ar: من حفظ عشر آيات من أول سورة الكهف عصم من الدجال  والاستعاذة بالله من فتنتة عقب التشهد الأخير من كل صلاة
items.text: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal; and also seeking refuge in Allah from his trial after the final tashahhud of every prayer.
items.src: Muslim 1/555; and in a narration: from the end of al-Kahf, 1/556.

chapters.title: Supplication for one who says: I love you for the sake of Allah
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء لمن قال إني أحبك في الله

items.ar: أحبك الذي أحببتني له ُ
items.text: May He for Whose sake you love me love you.
items.src: Abu Dawud 4/333; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih Sunan Abi Dawud 3/965.

chapters.title: Supplication for one who offers you his wealth

items.ar: بارك الله لك في أهلك ومالك
items.text: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth.
items.src: al-Bukhari (al-Fath) 4/88

chapters.title: Supplication for the lender when repaying a loan

items.ar: بارك الله لك في أهلك ومالك إنما جزاء السلف الحمد والأداء
items.text: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth. The recompense for a loan is only praise and repayment.
items.src: an-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah p. 300 and Ibn Majah 2/809; see Sahih Ibn Majah 2/809; see Sahih Ibn Majah 2/55.

chapters.title: Supplication out of fear of shirk

items.ar: اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن أشرك بك وأنا أعلم ، وأستغفرك لما لا أعلم
items.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.
items.src: Ahmad 4/403 and others; see Sahih al-Jami' 3/333 and Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib by al-Albani.

chapters.title: Supplication for one who says: May Allah bless you
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء لمن قال بارك الله فيك

items.ar: وفيك بارك الله
items.text: And may Allah bless you too.
items.src: Ibn as-Sunni p. 138 no. 278; see al-Wabil as-Sayyib by Ibn al-Qayyim, 304, edited by Bashir Muhammad Uyun.

chapters.title: Supplication against superstitious omens

items.ar: اللهم لا طير إلا طيرك ، ولا خير إلا خيرك ،ولا إله غيرك
items.text: O Allah, there is no omen except Your omen, no good except Your good, and no deity other than You.
items.src: Ahmad 2/220 and Ibn as-Sunni no. 292; al-Albani graded it sahih in al-Ahadith as-Sahihah 3/54 no. 1065. As for good omens (al-fa'l), they pleased the Prophet ﷺ; thus when he heard a good word from a man that pleased him, he said: «We have taken your good omen from your mouth.» Abu Dawud and Ahmad; al-Albani graded it sahih in as-Sahihah 2/363, (reported) by Abu ash-Shaykh in Akhlaq an-Nabi.

chapters.title: Supplication when mounting a riding animal

items.ar: بسم الله. الحمد لله. {سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ * وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ} الحمد لله ، الحمد لله ، الحمد لله ، الله اكبر ، الله اكبر ، الله اكبر ، سبحانك اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ، فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت
items.text: In the name of Allah. Praise be to Allah. «Glory be to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could not have done it ourselves. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.» Praise be to Allah, praise be to Allah, praise be to Allah. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. Glory be to You, O Allah! Indeed, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
items.src: Abu Dawud 3/34, at-Tirmidhi 5/501; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/156.

chapters.title: Supplication for travel

items.ar: الله أكبر، الله أكبر، الله أكبر،{سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ * وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ}  اللهم إنا نسألُكَ في سفرنا هذا البرَّ والتقوى، ومن العمل ما ترضى، اللهم هون علينا سفرنا هذا واطو عنا بعده، اللهم أنت الصاحب في السفر، والخليفة في الأهل، اللهم إني أعوذ بك من وعْثاءِ السفر، وكآبة المنظر وسوء المنقلب في المال والأهل وإذا رجع قالهن وزاد فيهن آيبون، تائبون، عابدون، لربنا حامدون
items.text: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. «Glory be to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could not have done it ourselves. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.» O Allah, we ask You in this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and for deeds that You are pleased with. O Allah, make this journey of ours easy for us and fold up its distance for us. O Allah, You are the Companion in travel and the Successor over the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, from a distressing sight, and from an evil return in wealth and family. And when he returned, he would say them and add: «We return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord.»
items.src: Muslim 2/978

chapters.title: Supplication upon entering a village or town

items.ar: اللهم رب السموات السبع وما أظللن ، ورب الأرضين السبع وما أقللن ،ورب الشياطين وما أضللن ، ورب الرياح وما ذرين.أسألك خير هذه القرية وخير أهلها ، وخير ما فيها،وأعوذ بك من شرها،وشر أهلها ، وشر ما فيها
items.text: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and all that they shade, Lord of the seven earths and all that they carry, Lord of the devils and all whom they misguide, Lord of the winds and all that they scatter! I ask You for the good of this town, the good of its people and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of its people and the evil of what is in it.
items.src: al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, and adh-Dhahabi agreed, 2/100; Ibn as-Sunni no. 524; al-Hafiz graded it hasan in Takhrij al-Adhkar 5/154. Ibn Baz said: «an-Nasa'i also reported it with a hasan chain.» See Tuhfat al-Akhyar p. 37.

chapters.title: Supplication upon entering the market

items.ar: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، له الملك وله الحمد ، يُحيي ويُميت ، وهو حي لا يموت ، بيده الخير وهو على كل شئ قدير
items.text: There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and does not die. In His Hand is all good, and He is over all things capable.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/491, al-Hakim 1/538; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih Ibn Majah 2/21 and in Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/152.

chapters.title: Supplication when the mount stumbles

items.ar: بسم الله
items.text: In the name of Allah.
items.src: Abu Dawud 4/296; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih Abi Dawud 3/941.

chapters.title: Supplication of the traveller for the one staying behind

items.ar: أستودعُكَ الله الذي لا تضيع ودائعه
items.text: I entrust you to Allah, Whose trusts are never lost.
items.src: Ahmad 2/403, Ibn Majah 2/943; see Sahih Ibn Majah 2/133.

chapters.title: Supplication of the one staying behind for the traveller

items.ar: أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك ،وخواتيم عملك
items.text: I entrust to Allah your religion, your trustworthiness, and the final outcomes of your deeds.
items.src: Ahmad 2/7, at-Tirmidhi 5/499; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/155.

items.ar: زوَّدك الله التقوى، وغفر ذْنبك ويسَّر لك الخير حيث ما كنت
items.text: May Allah provide you with piety as provision, forgive your sin, and make good easy for you wherever you are.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/155.

chapters.title: Takbir and tasbih while travelling

items.ar: قال جابر رضي الله عنه :  كنا إذا صعدنا كبرنا ، وإذا نزلنا سبحنا
items.text: Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) said: «When we ascended, we would say takbir, and when we descended, we would say tasbih».
items.src: al-Bukhari (al-Fath) 6/135

chapters.title: Supplication of the traveller before dawn

items.ar: سَمعَ سَامعً بحمد الله وحُسنِ بلائه علينا، ربنا صاحبنا ، وأفضِل علينا عائذا بالله من النار
items.text: A hearer has heard our praise of Allah and His good favour upon us. Our Lord, be with us and bestow Your favour upon us, (I say this) seeking refuge with Allah from the Fire.
items.src: Muslim 4/2086. The meaning of «a hearer has heard»: a witness has borne witness to our praise of Allah the Exalted for His blessings and His good favour. (Another) meaning of «a hearer has heard»: let the one who hears this saying of mine convey it to others and say the like of it, as a reminder of remembrance and supplication before dawn. His saying «Our Lord, be with us and bestow favour upon us» means: protect us, guard us, watch over us, bestow upon us Your abundant blessings and avert from us every harm. Sharh an-Nawawi 17/39.

chapters.title: Supplication when stopping at a place, during travel or otherwise
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء إذا نزل منزلا في سفر أو غيره

items.ar: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات من شر ما خلق
items.text: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
items.src: Muslim 4/2080

chapters.title: Remembrance upon returning from travel

items.ar: يكبر على كل شرف ثلاث تكبيرات ثم يقول : لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك لهُ ،لهُ الملك ، ولهُ الحمدُ وهو على كل شيءٍ قدير ، آيبون ،تائبون ، عابدون ، لربنا حامدون ،صدق الله وعده،ونصر عبده،وهزم الأحزاب وحده
items.text: He says takbir three times upon every elevated place, then says: «There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable. We return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord. Allah has fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone».
items.src: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it when returning from a military expedition or Hajj. al-Bukhari 7/163, Muslim 2/980.

chapters.title: What one says and does when something pleasing or displeasing happens
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول ويفعل من أتاه أمر يسره أو يكرهه

items.ar: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه الأمر يسره قال : الحمد لله الذي بنعمته تتم الصالحات  و إذا أتاه أمر يكرهه قال :  الحمد لله على كل حال
items.text: When something pleasing came to him ﷺ, he would say: «Praise be to Allah, by Whose favour good things are completed». And when something displeasing came to him, he would say: «Praise be to Allah in every situation».
items.src: Ibn as-Sunni in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah, and al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, 1/499; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih al-Jami' 4/201.

chapters.title: The virtue of sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ
chapters.titleAr: فضل الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

items.ar: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم  من صلى علي صلاة صلى الله عليه بها عشراً
items.text: He ﷺ said: «Whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten blessings upon him for it».
items.src: Muslim 1/288

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم :  لا تجعلوا قبري عيداً وصلوا علي ؛ فإن صلاتكم تبلغني حيث كنتم
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Do not make my grave a place of festivity, and send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are».
items.src: Abu Dawud 2/218, Ahmad 2/367; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih Abi Dawud 2/383.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم :  البخيل من ذكرت عندهُ فلم يصل علي
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me».
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/551 and others; see Sahih al-Jami' 3/25 and Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/177.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم  إن لله ملائكة سياحين في الأرض يبلغوني من أمتي السلام
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Allah has angels who roam the earth, conveying to me the greetings of peace from my Ummah».
items.src: an-Nasa'i and al-Hakim 2/421; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih an-Nasa'i 1/274.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم  ما من أحدٍ يسلِّمُ عليَّ إلَّا ردَّ اللَّهُ عليَّ روحي حتَّى أردَّ عليْهِ السَّلامَ
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «No one sends greetings of peace upon me but Allah returns my soul to me so that I may return his greeting».
items.src: Abu Dawud no. 2041; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/383.

chapters.title: Spreading the greeting of peace

items.ar: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : لا تدخلوا الجنة حتى تؤمنوا ، ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا ، أو لا أدلكم على شيءٍ إذا فعلتموه تحاببتم ، أفشوا السلام بينكم
items.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among yourselves».
items.src: Muslim 1/74 and others

items.ar: ثلاث من جمعهن فقد جمع الإيمان : الإنصاف من نفسك ، وبذل السلام للعالم ،والإنفاق من الإقتار
items.text: Three things, whoever combines them has combined faith: being fair from your own self, offering the greeting of peace to everyone, and spending despite scarcity.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 1/82, from Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him), as mawquf and mu'allaq.

items.ar: وعن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما : أن رجلاً سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الإسلام خير قال : تطعم الطعام وتقرأ السلام على من عرفت ومن لم تعرف
items.text: From Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both): A man asked the Prophet ﷺ: «Which (deed of) Islam is best?» He said: «That you feed (others) and give the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know».
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 1/55, Muslim 1/65

chapters.title: How to return the greeting of a disbeliever
chapters.titleAr: كيف يرد السلام على الكافر إذا سلم

items.ar: إذا سلم عليكم أهل الكتاب فقولوا :  وعليكم
items.text: When the People of the Book greet you, say: «And upon you».
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 11/42, Muslim 4/1705

chapters.title: Supplication upon hearing a rooster crow or a donkey bray

items.ar: إذا سمعتم صياح الديكة ، فاسألوا الله من فضله فإنها رأت ملكاً وإذا سمعتم نهيق الحمار ، فتعوذوا بالله من الشيطان فإنه رأى شيطاناً
items.text: When you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah for His bounty, for they have seen an angel. And when you hear the braying of a donkey, seek refuge in Allah from the Shaytan, for it has seen a devil.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 6/350, Muslim 4/2092

chapters.title: Supplication upon hearing dogs bark at night

items.ar: إذا سمعتم نُباح الكلاب ونهيق الحمير بالليل فتعوذوا بالله منهن فإنهن يرين ما لا ترون
items.text: When you hear the barking of dogs and the braying of donkeys at night, seek refuge in Allah from them, for they see what you do not see.
items.src: Abu Dawud 4/327, Ahmad 3/306; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih Abi Dawud 3/961.

chapters.title: Supplication for one whom you have reviled

items.ar: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم:  اللَّهُم فأيما مؤمن سببته فاجعل ذلك له قربة إليك يوم القيامة
items.text: He ﷺ said: «O Allah, whichever believer I have reviled, make that a means of nearness to You for him on the Day of Resurrection».
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 11/171 and Muslim 4/2007, whose wording is: «make it for him a purification and a mercy».

chapters.title: What a Muslim says when praising a Muslim
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول المسلم إذا مدح المسلم

items.ar: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم :  إذا كان أحدكم مادحاً صاحبه لا محالة فليقل : أحسبُ فلاناً والله حسيبهُ ولا أزكي على الله أحداً ، أحسبهُ – إن كان يعلم ذاك – كذا وكذا
items.text: He ﷺ said: «If one of you must praise his companion, let him say: I consider so-and-so (to be such), and Allah is his Reckoner, and I do not attest to anyone's purity before Allah; I consider him, if he knows that, to be such and such».
items.src: Muslim 4/2296

chapters.title: What a Muslim says when he is praised

items.ar: اللهم لا تؤاخذني بما يقولون ، واغفر لي مالا يعلمون [واجعلني خيراً مما يظنون]
items.text: O Allah, do not take me to account for what they say, and forgive me for what they do not know [and make me better than what they think].
items.src: al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad no. 761; al-Albani graded its chain sahih in Sahih al-Adab al-Mufrad no. 585; what is between the square brackets is an addition by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman 4/228 via another chain.

chapters.title: How the pilgrim in ihram says the talbiyah in Hajj or Umrah
chapters.titleAr: كيف يلبي المحرم في الحج أو العمرة

items.ar: لبيك اللهم لبيك ، لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك ، إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك ، لا شريك لك
items.text: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed, all praise, blessing and dominion belong to You. You have no partner.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 3/408, Muslim 2/841

chapters.title: Takbir upon reaching the Black Stone corner

items.ar: طاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالبيت على بعير كلما أتي الركن أشار إليه بشيء عنده وكبر
items.text: The Prophet ﷺ performed tawaf around the House on a camel; every time he came to the Corner, he pointed to it with something he had with him and said takbir.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 3/476; what is meant by «something» is the mihjan (a staff with a curved end); see al-Bukhari with al-Fath 3/472.

chapters.title: Supplication between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone
chapters.titleAr: الدعاء بين الركن اليماني والحجر الأسود

items.ar: { رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ}
items.text: «Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.»
items.src: Abu Dawud 2/179, Ahmad 3/411, and al-Baghawi in Sharh as-Sunnah 7/128; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih Abi Dawud 1/354; the verse is from Surat al-Baqarah, 201.

chapters.title: Supplication when standing on as-Safa and al-Marwah

items.ar: فلما دنا صلى الله عليه وسلم من الصفا قرأ: { إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ اللّهِ }  أبدأ بما بدأ الله به  فبدأ بالصفا فرقي عليه حتى رأى البيت فاستقبل القبلة ، فوحد الله وكبره وقال :  لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك لهُ ، لهُ الملك ولهُ الحمد وهو على كل شيءٍ قدير ، لا إله إلا الله وحده ، أنجز وعده ، ونصر عبده ، وهزم الأحزاب وحده  ثم دعا بين ذلك . قال مثل هذا ثلاث مرات  الحديث وفيه  ففعل على المروة كما فعل على الصفا
items.text: When he ﷺ drew near to as-Safa, he recited: «Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah». «I begin with what Allah began with». So he began with as-Safa and climbed it until he saw the House; he faced the qiblah, declared the Oneness of Allah and magnified Him, and said: «There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable. There is no deity except Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone». Then he supplicated in between that. He said the like of this three times. The hadith, and in it: «He did on al-Marwah as he had done on as-Safa».
items.src: Muslim 2/888

chapters.title: Supplication on the Day of Arafah

items.ar: خير الدعاء دعاء يوم عرفة ، وخيرُ ما قلت أنا والنبيُّون من قبلي : لا إله إلا الله وحدهُ لا شريك لهُ ، لهُ الملكُ ولهُ الحمدُ وهو على كل شيء قدير
items.text: The best supplication is the supplication of the Day of Arafah, and the best that I and the prophets before me have said is: «There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable».
items.src: at-Tirmidhi; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/184, and in as-Sahihah 4/6.

chapters.title: Remembrance at al-Mash'ar al-Haram

items.ar: ركب صلى الله عليه وسلم القصواء حتى أتى المشعر الحرام فاستقبل القبلة ( فدعاه ُ، وكبرهُ ،وهللهُ ، ووحدهُ) فلم يزل واقفاً حتى أسفر جداً فدفع قبل أن تطلع الشمس
items.text: He ﷺ rode al-Qaswa' until he came to al-Mash'ar al-Haram; he faced the qiblah (and supplicated to Him, magnified Him, declared that there is no deity but Him and declared His Oneness), and he remained standing until it became very bright, then he moved on before the sun rose.
items.src: Muslim 2/891

chapters.title: Takbir with every pebble when stoning the Jamarat
chapters.titleAr: التكبيرة عند رمي الجمار مع كل حصاة

items.ar: يكبر كلما رمى بحصاة عند الجمار الثلاث ثم يتقدم، ويقف يدعو مستقبل القبلة، رافعاً يديه بعد الجمرة الأولى والثانية، أما جمرة العقبة فيرميها ويكبر عند كل حصاة وينصرف ولا يقف عندها
items.text: He says takbir each time he throws a pebble at the three Jamarat, then he steps forward and stands supplicating, facing the qiblah and raising his hands, after the first and second Jamrah. As for Jamrat al-Aqabah, he stones it, saying takbir with every pebble, and leaves without standing at it.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 3/583 and 3/584, see its wording there; and al-Bukhari with al-Fath 3/581; Muslim also reported it.

chapters.title: What to say when amazed or upon something pleasing
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول عند التعجب والأمر السار

items.ar: سبحان الله
items.text: Glory be to Allah!
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 1/210, 390 and 414, Muslim 4/1857

items.ar: الله أكبر
items.text: Allah is the Greatest!
items.src: al-Bukhari (al-Fath) 8/441; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2/103 and 2/235, and Musnad Ahmad 5/218.

chapters.title: What one does when something pleasing happens
chapters.titleAr: ما يفعل من أتاه أمر يسره

items.ar: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه أمر يسرهُ أو يسرُّ به خر ساجداً شكراً لله تبارك وتعالى
items.text: When something pleasing came to the Prophet ﷺ, or he was given glad news of something, he would fall down in prostration out of gratitude to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
items.src: Reported by the compilers of the Sunan except an-Nasa'i. See Sahih Ibn Majah 1/233 and Irwa' al-Ghalil 2/226.

chapters.title: What to say when feeling pain in the body
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول من أحس وجعاً في جسده

items.ar: ضع يدك على الذي تألم من جسدك وقل: بسم الله ، ثلاثاً  وقل سبع مرات :  أعوذ بالله وقدرته من شر ما أجد وأحاذر
items.text: Place your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say: «In the name of Allah» three times, and say seven times: «I seek refuge in Allah and His Power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear».
items.src: Muslim 4/1728

chapters.title: Supplication of one who fears harming something with his (evil) eye
chapters.titleAr: دعاء من خشي أن يصيب شيئاً بعينه

items.ar: إذا رأى أحدكم من أخيه ، أو من نفسه ، أومن ماله ما يعجبهُ [فليدع لهُ بالبركة ] فإن العين حقٌّ
items.text: When one of you sees something in his brother, or in himself, or in his wealth that pleases him, [let him supplicate for blessing for it], for the evil eye is real.
items.src: Musnad Ahmad 4/447, Ibn Majah and Malik; al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih al-Jami' 1/212; see al-Arna'ut's edition of Zad al-Ma'ad 4/170.

chapters.title: What is said when frightened

items.ar: لا إله إلا الله
items.text: There is no deity except Allah.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 6/181, Muslim 4/2208

chapters.title: What to say when slaughtering or sacrificing
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول عند الذبح أو النحر

items.ar: بسم الله والله أكبر [ اللهم منك ولك ] اللهم تقبل مني
items.text: In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. [O Allah, (it is) from You and for You.] O Allah, accept (it) from me.
items.src: Muslim 3/1557 and al-Bayhaqi 9/287; what is between the square brackets is in al-Bayhaqi 9/287 and others; the last sentence I have given by meaning from Muslim's narration.

chapters.title: What to say to repel the plotting of the rebellious devils
chapters.titleAr: ما يقول لرد كيد مردة الشياطين

items.ar: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات التي لا يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما خلق ، وبرأ وذرأ ومن شر ما ينزل من السماء ، ومن شر ما يعرج فيها ، ومن شر ما ذرأ في الأرض ، ومن شر ما يخرج منها ، ومن شر فتن الليل والنهار ، ومن شر كل طارق إلا طارقاً يطرق بخير يا رحمن
items.text: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can go beyond, from the evil of what He has created, brought into being and spread; from the evil of what descends from the sky and the evil of what ascends into it; from the evil of what He has spread in the earth and the evil of what comes out of it; from the evil of the trials of the night and the day; and from the evil of every night visitor, except a night visitor who comes with good, O Most Merciful!
items.src: Ahmad 3/419 with a sahih chain, and Ibn as-Sunni no. 637; al-Arna'ut graded its chain sahih in his takhrij of at-Tahawiyyah p. 133; see Majma' az-Zawa'id 10/127.

chapters.title: Seeking forgiveness and repentance

items.ar: قال رسول الله صلى الله عيه وسلم : والله إني لاستغفر الله وأتوب إليه في اليوم أكثر من سبعين مرة
items.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times a day».
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 11/101

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : يا أيها الناس توبوا إلى الله فإني أتوب في اليوم إليه مائة مرةً
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him a hundred times a day».
items.src: Muslim 4/2076

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : من قال أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ، غفر الله لهُ وإن كان فر من الزحف
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Whoever says: “I seek the forgiveness of Allah the Magnificent, besides Whom there is no deity, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all, and I repent to Him”, Allah will forgive him, even if he had fled from the battlefield».
items.src: Abu Dawud 2/85, at-Tirmidhi 5/569, and al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, and adh-Dhahabi agreed, 1/511; al-Albani graded it sahih. See Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/182 and Jami' al-Usul li-Ahadith ar-Rasul ﷺ 4/389–390, edited by al-Arna'ut.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : أقرب ما يكون الربُّ من العبد في جوف الليل الآخر فإن استطعت أن تكون ممن يذكر الله في تلك الساعة فكن
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «The closest the Lord is to the servant is in the last part of the night; so if you are able to be among those who remember Allah at that hour, then be».
items.src: at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i 1/279 and al-Hakim; see Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/183 and Jami' al-Usul, edited by al-Arna'ut, 4/144.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد فأكثروا الدعاء
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so increase in supplication».
items.src: Muslim 1/350

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : إنه ليغان على قلبي وإني لاستغفرُ الله في اليوم مائة مرة
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Indeed, my heart becomes clouded, and indeed I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day».
items.src: Muslim 4/2075. Ibn al-Athir said: «(my heart becomes clouded) means it is covered and overcast. What is meant is inattentiveness, because he ﷺ was continually increasing in remembrance, nearness (to Allah) and constant vigilance; so when he became inattentive to any of that at some times, or forgot, he counted it as a sin upon himself and hastened to seek forgiveness». See Jami' al-Usul 4/386.

chapters.title: The virtue of glorifying, praising, declaring the Oneness of, and magnifying Allah

items.ar: قال صلى الله عيه وسلم من قال سبحان الله وبحمده في يوم مائة مرة حطت خطاياه ولو كانت مثل زبد البحر
items.text: He ﷺ said: «Whoever says “Glory be to Allah and with His praise” a hundred times a day, his sins will be wiped away even if they are like the foam of the sea».
items.src: al-Bukhari 7/168, Muslim 4/2071; see: the virtue of one who says it a hundred times in the morning and evening.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : من قال لا إله إلا وحده لا شريك لهُ ، لهُ الملك ، ولهُ الحمدُ ، وهو على كل شيء قدير عشر مرات . كان كمن أعتق أربعة أنفس من ولد إسماعيل
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Whoever says ten times: “There is no deity except (Allah) alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable”, will be like one who freed four souls from the descendants of Isma'il».
items.src: al-Bukhari 7/67, and Muslim with this wording 4/2071; see the virtue of one who says it a hundred times a day.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم : كلمتان خفيفتان على اللسان ، ثقيلتان في الميزان حبيبتان إلى الرحمن : سبحان الله وبحمده سبحان الله العظيم
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah the Magnificent».
items.src: al-Bukhari 7/167, Muslim 4/2072

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم  : لأن أقول سبحان الله ، والحمد لله ،ولا إله إلا الله ، والله أكبر ،أحب إلى مما طلعت عليه الشمس
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «That I say: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, is more beloved to me than everything the sun has risen upon».
items.src: Muslim 4/2072

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم: أيعجز أحدكم أن يكسب كل يوم ألف حسنةفسأله سائل من جلسائه كيف يكسب أحدنا ألف حسنة ؟ قال : يسبح مائة تسبيحة ، فيكتب له ألف حسنة أو يحط عنه ُ ألف خطيئة
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «Is any one of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds every day?» One of those sitting with him asked: «How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds?» He said: «He glorifies (Allah) a hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are written for him, or a thousand sins are wiped away from him».
items.src: Muslim 4/2073

items.ar: من قال سبحان الله العظيم وبحمده غرست له نخلة في الجنة
items.text: Whoever says: «Glory be to Allah the Magnificent and with His praise», a palm tree is planted for him in Paradise.
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/511, al-Hakim 1/501, who graded it sahih, and adh-Dhahabi agreed; see Sahih al-Jami' 5/531 and Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/160.

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم: يا عبد الله بن قيس ألا أدلك على كنز من كنوز الجنة ؟ فقلت:بلى يا رسول الله ، قال : قل لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «O Abdullah ibn Qays, shall I not direct you to a treasure among the treasures of Paradise?» I said: «Yes, O Messenger of Allah». He said: «Say: There is no might nor power except by Allah».
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 11/213, Muslim 4/2076

items.ar: وقال صلى الله عيه وسلم: أحب الكلام إلى الله أربعٌ : سبحان الله ، والحمد لله ، ولا إله إلا الله ، والله أكبر ، لا يضرك بأيهنَّ بدأت
items.text: And he ﷺ said: «The most beloved words to Allah are four: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. It does not harm you with which of them you begin».
items.src: Muslim 3/1685

items.ar: جاء أعرابي إلى رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فقال: علمني كلاماً أقوله : قال  قل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك لهً ،الله أكبرُ كبيراً ، والحمد لله كثيراً ، سبحان الله رب العالمين ،لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العزيز الحكيم  قال فهؤلاء لربي فما لي ؟ قال :  قل: اللهم اغفر لي ،وارحمني ،واهدني وارزقني
items.text: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: «Teach me words to say». He said: «Say: There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. Allah is the Greatest, most great; abundant praise be to Allah; glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; there is no might nor power except by Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise». He said: «These are for my Lord, so what is for me?» He said: «Say: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me and provide for me».
items.src: Muslim 4/2072; Abu Dawud added: «When the Bedouin turned away, the Prophet ﷺ said: He has filled his hands with good», 1/220.

items.ar: كان الرجل إذا أسلم علمه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة ثم أمره أن يدعو بهؤلاء الكلمات : اللهم اغفر لي، وارحمني ،واهدني ، وعافني وارزقني
items.text: When a man embraced Islam, the Prophet ﷺ would teach him the prayer, then command him to supplicate with these words: «O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being and provide for me».
items.src: Muslim 4/2073; and in a narration of Muslim: «For these combine for you your worldly life and your Hereafter».

items.ar: إن أفضل الذكر لا إله إلا الله
items.text: Indeed, the best remembrance is: «There is no deity except Allah».
items.src: at-Tirmidhi 5/462, Ibn Majah 2/1249, and al-Hakim 1/503, who graded it sahih, and adh-Dhahabi agreed; see Sahih al-Jami' 1/362.

items.ar: الباقيات الصالحات : سبحان الله والحمد لله ، ولا إله إلا الله ،والله أكبر ،و لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
items.text: The enduring good deeds: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no deity except Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no might nor power except by Allah.
items.src: Ahmad no. 513 in Ahmad Shakir's arrangement, and its chain is sahih; see Majma' az-Zawa'id 1/297. Ibn Hajar, in Bulugh al-Maram, attributed it from the narration of Abu Sa'id to an-Nasa'i and said: «Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim graded it sahih».

chapters.title: How did the Prophet ﷺ make tasbih?
chapters.titleAr: كيف كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسبح ؟

items.ar: عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما قال :  رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعقد التسبيح بيمينه
items.text: Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: «I saw the Prophet ﷺ counting tasbih on his right hand».
items.src: Abu Dawud with this wording 2/81, at-Tirmidhi 5/521; see Sahih al-Jami' 4/271 no. 4865.

chapters.title: Some kinds of good and comprehensive etiquette

items.ar: إذا كان جنح الليل – أو أمسيتم – فكفوا صبيانكم ؛ فإن الشياطين تنتشر حينئذ ، فإذا ذهب ساعة من الليل فخلوهم ،وأغلقوا الأبواب واذكروا اسم الله ؛ فإن الشيطان لا يفتح باباً مغلقاً ، وأوكوا قربكم واذكروا اسم الله ، وخمروا آنيتكم واذكروا اسم الله ، ولو أن تعرضوا عليها شيئاً ، وأطفئوا مصابيحكم
items.text: When the darkness of night falls, or (he said) when evening comes, keep your children in, for the devils spread out at that time. When an hour of the night has passed, let them go. Close the doors and mention the name of Allah, for the Shaytan does not open a closed door. Tie up your waterskins and mention the name of Allah. Cover your vessels and mention the name of Allah, even if only by placing something across them. And put out your lamps.
items.src: al-Bukhari with al-Fath 10/88, Muslim 3/1595
